objective: Test whether a syntactically small exact deferred transformation wrapper can hide exponential future query work, and whether a locally certified projection can eliminate that debt when available.
family: UNIT_EXISTS_TRAP_k: F_k(q)=AND_i q_i, with every q_i existentially quantified; projected semantics EXISTS Q F_k is TRUE.

LAZY_EXISTS_V0.size_proxy: source literal count + quantified-variable list + one wrapper node
LAZY_EXISTS_V0.evaluator: lexicographically enumerate Q assignments from all-zero to all-one and stop on first satisfying extension
LAZY_EXISTS_V0.expected_debt: all-one is the unique satisfying extension, hence exactly 2^k extension checks

EAGER_UNIT_PROJECT_V1.representation: scan quantified positive unit clauses, discharge each exact existential unit, emit TRUE
EAGER_UNIT_PROJECT_V1.work_proxy: literal/unit scans + k local projection certificates

gates.G1_EXACT_SEMANTICS: lazy and eager candidates both agree with exact projected truth
gates.G3_DEFERRED_DEBT_SIGNATURE: lazy evaluator performs exactly 2^k extension checks on every frozen k
gates.G4_EAGER_LOCAL_ESCAPE: eager exact projection work <=4k and emits TRUE
gates.G5_DEBT_ACCOUNTING: lazy query work is never erased because wrapper syntax is small
gates.G6_SCIENTIFIC_BOUNDARY: this refutes only LAZY_EXISTS_V0 as tractable interface; it does not refute all deferred representations or prove a universal eager projection

external_boundary.relevance: Structured d-DNNF can suffer superpolynomial blow-up under existential quantification, showing that transformation closure is a genuine representation-language issue beyond this simple trap.

journal_rule: Store syntax size, exact extension checks, eager projection work, semantic result, debt ratio, external bridge and next stronger closure-hardness target append-only.
